name: Global Ensemble Forecast Request Builder Nodes
description: Request-builder flow nodes for a machine-learned global ensemble weather forecast source served as Zarr v3 objects from an allow-listed cloud bucket. A module cron TIMER tick enters on 'tick'; plan emits one hostcap/http-request GET per (cloud-cover array x lead x chunk) as a raw-body-v1 request together with the positional per-chunk parse job for weathernext-parser:parse_cloud_chunks; cyclone_request emits the tropical-cyclone track CSV fetch plus its job; publish_request turns a completed storage-ingest result plus the parser's ingest meta into the dataset-publication POST for the node's loopback admin endpoint, emitting nothing when weathernext_publish_url is unset. EVERYTHING is node CONFIG through the builtin plugin.getConfig hostcall: weathernext_live_access is the live switch (default false: no request, no job, no secrets.get, one status frame {skipped: live-access-disabled}); weathernext_auth_mode none|bearer|refresh-token (bearer reads the operator's OAuth2 access token from the machine-bound credential store lane weathernext_secrets_lane through secrets.get and places it ONLY on the request frames, never on a job frame, wiping it after use; refresh-token is reserved and reports auth-mode-unsupported); the store path, arrays, init time, leads, chunk indices, chunk shape, codecs, dimension order, dtype and grid are all operator-declared because anonymous reads of the bucket are refused and its layout could not be verified. Licence class is decided per (init, lead) from valid time against the clock: at least one hour old is Historical (open attribution licence), otherwise RealTimeExperimental (experimental real-time terms). This is the ONLY node in the flow holding the credential capability, so the parser sibling stays capabilities:[] and browser-instantiable; every rebuild changes this artifact's hash and revokes the operator's secrets approval for it by design.

sequentialJustification.detail: One method over one control frame: read the node config, make at most a handful of synchronous hostcalls in a fixed order (plugin.getConfig, then secrets.get in bearer mode), emit request and job frames. No shared mutable state, no worker pool, no fan-out inside the guest. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles the single-thread lane rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Turns one timer tick into N raw-body-v1 http request frames and N positional chunk jobs, one pair per (array x lead x chunk index pair) from node CONFIG, or one status frame when weathernext_live_access is false / the store path is missing. Chunk key layout: <base>/<store_path>/<array>/c/<init_index>/<member_index>/<lead_index>/<latChunk>/<lonChunk> with lead_index = lead_hours / weathernext_lead_step_hours. BATCHING: the tick port is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE, not merely declared. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime - space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node whole queue port-blind up to the drain budget (64) - so a second tick in one invocation would emit one plan for two ticks. A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

wildcardJustification.detail: Cron timer tick frame produced by the flow runtime and consumed inside this flow only; it carries no payload of its own, so there is no SDS record to name.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON for hostcap/http-request: {"method":"GET","url","headers"?,"timeoutMs","responseWire":"raw-body-v1"}, one per chunk.

wildcardJustification.detail: hostcap/http-request request descriptor ({method,url,headers,timeoutMs,responseWire}) produced and consumed inside this flow; its shape is defined by the host http.request op, not by SDS. In bearer mode it carries the authorization header and travels only to the http node.

outputPorts.description: One chunk fetch request per (array x lead x chunk); ABSENT when live access is disabled.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON chunk job for weathernext-parser:parse_cloud_chunks, positionally aligned with the request frames.

outputPorts.description: One parse job per request frame, in the same order; ABSENT when live access is disabled.

methods.description: Turns a completed ingest (storage-ingest result + parser meta) into the loopback dataset-publication POST for hostcap/http-request. Emits nothing unless node CONFIG carries weathernext_publish_url — absence of configuration is not permission to publish. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE; a second result in one invocation would publish one record for two ingests, attributing the wrong meta to the wrong result, so a surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count. See graph task modules-guest-nodes-drop-batched-frames.

inputPorts.description: Parser ingest meta for the same batch.
